statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-mode audit of eight representative public routes. Authenticated dashboards, successful real-data form submission, account management, application-partner portals and every localized variant were not covered.

page.framework: WordPress marketing MPA; separate server-rendered React login surface
page.notes: Public education identity platform with marketing, content, signup and login journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot or computed background under an emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark condition will reveal whether surfaces re-tint; the page CSS / a color-scheme declaration is corroborating evidence. The model chooses the method.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The light and dark preference screenshots are pixel-identical (425,026 bytes each); white surfaces remain white under prefers-color-scheme: dark.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video, or an in-page probe of getAnimations()/computed animation under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce condition, can show whether motion stops. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Reduced-motion probe found zero active animations and a prefers-reduced-motion CSS rule.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot under emulated prefers-contrast: more / forced-colors, or an axe/contrast probe, can show whether controls and text survive. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Forced-colors plus prefers-contrast screenshot retained visible text, links and control outlines.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video of a route/state change shows whether it animates; the page source / ::view-transition usage corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM and CSS inspection across the WordPress templates found no view-transition-name or cross-document @view-transition rule.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from representative route and interaction recon.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The inspected templates do not contain parallax, scrollytelling, reveal or other scroll-linked motion that would require a scroll timeline.
checkOutcomes.reason: The inspected templates do not contain parallax, scrollytelling, reveal or other scroll-linked motion that would require a scroll timeline.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for scroll-snap / overscroll-behavior / physics-based easing vs custom pointermove listeners. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS probe found scroll-snap-type and no evidence of pointermove-driven gesture overrides on inspected journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video of scrolling, or CSS inspection for scroll-state container queries. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshots and CSS inspection show a static header across pages as long as 12,536 CSS pixels, with no progress indicator or scroll-state query.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for anchor-name / position-anchor / position-try on overlays; a screenshot of an open overlay near a viewport edge can show drift. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM inspection shows nested custom ul/div/button menus; no anchor-name, position-anchor, popover, dialog, or details primitives were present.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for ::highlight / scroll-marker; a transition video can show whether attention is cued after navigation. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Page headings, selected tab treatments, large labelled CTAs and visible menu state consistently direct attention.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot on load, or a DOM probe for full-viewport overlays present before interaction. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All first-load screenshots show content immediately with no interstitial or obscuring consent wall.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/source inspection for popover / <dialog> / <details> vs custom overlay divs with manual dismiss handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The platform probe found zero dialog, popover and details elements; Lighthouse also found invalid direct div/button children in submenu lists.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot plus layout metrics can show the proportion of the viewport given to chrome vs content. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first view is content-led with a single compact header and generous whitespace; no application frame crowds the page.

checkOutcomes.method: layout metrics (scrollWidth vs innerWidth) and a screenshot at an emulated narrow mobile viewport reveal overflow. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All five marketing templates reported 360 px scroll width at a 360 px viewport and zero horizontal overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for @container / container-type; a computed-style probe of the same component in a wide vs narrow container shows whether it adapts. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection across rendered templates found no @container rule even though cards, tabs and navigation components recur in multiple widths.

checkOutcomes.method: a focus probe (focus an element, read the computed outline) or an axe target-size check; a screenshot of a focused control corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The evaluate probe found many visible links with 16 to 19 pixel boxes and social links 27 by 19 pixels, below robust touch-target guidance.

checkOutcomes.method: screenshot the first viewport and key scrolled states; inspect heading structure, nav labels, button text, and visual hierarchy; a task walkthrough can show whether the next action is obvious. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage, school, pricing and signup screenshots use specific headings and visually dominant next actions.

checkOutcomes.method: run the flow manually with screenshots/DOM snapshots at each step; compare expected vs actual path length; inspect form requirements, navigation continuity, and blockers. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The primary marketing journey reaches the district signup form and the student journey reaches a dedicated Badge/Password login chooser without a dead-end.

checkOutcomes.method: exercise network delay/failure, invalid input, empty data and success states; screenshot the state messaging and recovery controls; inspect whether browser history and focus remain sensible. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All visually required fields reported required=false and empty validationMessage; clicking submit left the captured viewport unchanged.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse reports LCP/CLS/TBT directly and the model may run it; layout metrics + a layout-shift observer + a long-task observer (the evidence primitives) give the same signal first-party. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.2 s and CLS 0.226, with performance 52; the trace separately measured LCP 3.65 s on a faster desktop run.

checkOutcomes.method: the layout primitive's CLS observer captures shifts; a transition video of the first seconds shows content jumping. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured cumulative layout shift 0.226. The short layout observer measured 0, indicating the shift occurs outside that observer window, not that it is absent.

checkOutcomes.method: the layout primitive records long tasks; a heap summary shows the object population; Lighthouse reports TBT. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reported interactive at 17.1 s and 434 KiB estimated unused JavaScript; TBT was only 80 ms and the trace saw no long tasks.

checkOutcomes.method: a HAR summary can reveal cache headers, redirects, render-blocking candidates, weight offenders and dependency shape; a trace/Lighthouse insight report can corroborate LCP discovery, render-blocking, font-display and document latency. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR recorded 68 requests and 3.92 MB transferred, including seven parser-blocking stylesheets and parser-inserted scripts; the largest image alone transferred 1.08 MB.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse/trace/code-coverage style evidence can flag unused JS/CSS, duplicated JavaScript and legacy code; a HAR summary shows third-party byte cost and request count. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 434 KiB unused JavaScript and 31 KiB unused CSS, including 67% waste in the theme script and 86% in theme CSS.

checkOutcomes.method: axe-core (injectable via the evaluate primitive) or Lighthouse's a11y audits enumerate these; a DOM probe of the accessibility-relevant attributes is a first-party alternative. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse home image-alt passed and the signup probe found labels for visible controls; login method cards have explicit aria-labels.

checkOutcomes.method: axe contrast rules, a Lighthouse contrast audit, or an in-page probe computing contrast ratios from computed colours. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast passed and forced-colors inspection preserved readable contrast.

checkOutcomes.method: axe/Lighthouse structural audits; a focus-walk probe (tab through, read activeElement + computed outline) is a first-party alternative. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found the form title jumps to h4 and multiple ul elements contain direct div or button children.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot of body and heading text, plus CSS inspection for text-wrap / text alignment / font fallback handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshots show comfortable type sizes, spacing and line lengths on desktop and mobile without clipping.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse/axe target-size, meta-viewport and media-caption audits are useful signals; screenshots at narrow and zoomed conditions plus DOM/media inspection can corroborate. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Viewport permits scaling to 5, all tested templates reflow without horizontal overflow, and no essential timed media appears in core views.

checkOutcomes.method: capture Runtime/Log CDP events, or a probe that reads collected errors; Lighthouse reports this too. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit passed with no items.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM/source probe for doctype/charset/img dimensions; CSS inspection for repetition; Lighthouse best-practices audits cover the rest. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The image primitive found 19 images without dimensions and 21 oversized images among 63 inspected; the logo natural width was 382 px for a 118 px display width.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices audits and DevTools inspector/deprecation signals can surface these; DOM/source probes can verify paste handlers and prompt timing. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse signup found three deprecated API warnings in the Cloudflare challenge script and a large first-party theme script without a source map.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM probe reads <title> and meta[name=description]; Lighthouse SEO audits cover the same ground. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The metadata probe returned title Clever and description null; Lighthouse SEO scored 92 and failed meta-description.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM probe for anchor hrefs, viewport meta, and robots; Lighthouse SEO audits corroborate. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse crawlable anchors and robots audits passed; viewport is present and the page has descriptive real links.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect response status and headers, <link rel=canonical>, hreflang links, robots meta, robots.txt and sitemap.xml; Lighthouse SEO audits cover several of these. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Main page returned 200, exposed a canonical URL and indexable robots policy; discoverability fetch succeeded.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect JSON-LD/microdata and social preview tags against visible content; Lighthouse has a manual structured-data audit, and ad-hoc probes can parse schema.org blocks. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The metadata probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags despite visible organization/product content.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect response headers / page protocol via an evaluate probe or the network layer; Lighthouse best-practices flags HTTPS and CSP issues. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; the cookies primitive found three Google analytics/visit cookies without Secure and all six cookies with SameSite=None.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect network requests and third-party origins; a probe of analytics/beacon calls. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Tracker evidence found seven third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and Analytics; HAR attributes 706 KB to third parties and Lighthouse signup observed DoubleClick.

checkOutcomes.method: a probe for permission requests fired on load; source inspection for passkey / WebAuthn / navigator.credentials usage in auth flows. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The login journey presented only Badge and Password cards; no permission prompt fired on load, and WebAuthn capability exists in the browser.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect response headers and browser security state; Lighthouse/DevTools security audits can corroborate HSTS, clickjacking, Trusted Types, origin isolation and third-party cookie findings. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The headers primitive found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP and HSTS.

checkOutcomes.method: load with scripting disabled or compare a no-JS fetch of the HTML against the rendered page; check for Baseline-aware fallbacks in source. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Discoverability measured 100% raw-HTML content coverage with title and H1 present and isJsShell=false.

checkOutcomes.method: exercise menus near viewport edges with a screenshot; a probe of async/visibility behaviour. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative menus, tabs, login chooser and form rendered without clipped active content at desktop/mobile sizes.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from representative route and interaction recon.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited public surface is a marketing/content MPA, not an installable app; authenticated product applications were outside this run.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public surface is a marketing/content MPA, not an installable app; authenticated product applications were outside this run.

checkOutcomes.method: simulate failed fetches/offline mode or inspect representative 404/500 routes; screenshots and DOM snapshots of error/loading/empty states show whether recovery is possible. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A nonexistent URL renders a titled 404 page with navigation and recovery links rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM probe for <html lang>/dir and CSS inspection for logical vs physical properties. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site links Canada, UK/Ireland, Australia/New Zealand and global variants and sets lang=en-US, but CSS inspection counted 1,003 physical left/right declarations and no dir strategy.

checkOutcomes.method: source inspection for Intl.* usage vs hand-rolled formatting; a probe of rendered dates/numbers under a different locale. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The article template displays OCTOBER 16, 2025 while the global navigation exposes several regions; no locale-aware metadata was observed in rendered output.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from representative route and interaction recon.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The inspected public marketing, pricing, signup and article templates expose no scheduling or cross-zone event workflow.
checkOutcomes.reason: The inspected public marketing, pricing, signup and article templates expose no scheduling or cross-zone event workflow.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot of consent/upsell/cancel flows; source inspection for declarative button actions vs misleading controls. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Pricing, signup and login views disclose audience, process, privacy/terms links and choices without confirmshaming or forced continuity.

checkOutcomes.method: exercise a form, submit invalid input, and observe timing and clarity of errors via a screenshot or a :user-invalid / aria-invalid probe. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The form probe found required=false for every visible field and no native validation messages after submit, undermining predictable and assistive error recovery.

checkOutcomes.method: source/DOM inspection for autocomplete attributes on form fields; a probe of autofill affordances. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Name, email, telephone, organization and country inputs all reported empty autocomplete; only a hidden company field used new-password.

checkOutcomes.method: walkthrough checkout/subscription/auth/account flows when present; screenshot pricing, confirmation, cancellation and reauthentication states; inspect passkey/autocomplete support for sign-in and payment. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The signup view explains four onboarding steps and exposes privacy/terms consent; login offers separate Badge, Password and Admin choices.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect transferred image bytes vs displayed size; source inspection for modern formats and resolution handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR recorded 2.62 MB of images; the image audit found 47 of 63 in legacy formats, 21 oversized and 25 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.

checkOutcomes.method: a long-task / network probe for background fetches and processing while idle or backgrounded. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse identified 434 KiB unused JavaScript and HAR recorded recaptcha, analytics, select2, PDF, Zoom and fancybox resources on the landing page.

checkOutcomes.method: a HAR summary shows third-party bytes, font/media weight and caching; screenshots/video reveal autoplay and decorative media; trace/layout evidence shows whether media/animation keeps work running. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR recorded 706 KB third-party transfer and 3.92 MB total, including 383 KB recaptcha script and 297 KB GTM before any form interaction.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from representative route and interaction recon.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No declared or evident intent to expose transactional capabilities to AI agents; this emerging capability is optional for the public marketing surface.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared or evident intent to expose transactional capabilities to AI agents; this emerging capability is optional for the public marketing surface.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from representative route and interaction recon.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarization or language-model task is part of the inspected core journeys, so on-device inference would add no clear user value.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarization or language-model task is part of the inspected core journeys, so on-device inference would add no clear user value.

checkOutcomes.method: compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes) across th
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten mobile-menu toggle attempts, heap self size rose only 165,213 bytes (0.72%) and node count 1,204 (0.31%), consistent with bounded startup variance rather than an unbounded leak.

checkOutcomes.method: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots and memlab snapshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline heap was 22.84 MB across 393,380 nodes for a 986-element marketing page; post-interaction remained 23.00 MB.

checkOutcomes.method: the `heap` summary by constructor (Detached* nodes) compared across a before/after pair shows a growing detached-DOM population; an `evaluate` probe can sample listener/timer counts (e.g. getEventListeners-style counting, or instrumenting addEventListener/setI
checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither heap summary exposed Detached constructors among top populations, and repeated toggling caused only small bounded count changes.

principleOutcomes.reason: No declared or evident intent to expose transactional capabilities to AI agents; this emerging capability is optional for the public marketing surface. No summarization or language-model task is part of the inspected core journeys, so on-device inference would add no clear user value.

paths.description: Homepage entry and primary CTA archetype; tested visual preferences, mobile reflow, performance, network, security, discoverability and memory.
School solution landing-page archetype with long-form product marketing and CTA.
Pricing/tabbed listing archetype and region/currency messaging.
Content listing and search/category navigation archetype.
Long-form article detail template with publication metadata and body content.
Primary district onboarding form journey; inspected labels, constraints, autocomplete, error behavior and accessibility.
Primary student authentication entry and auth-method chooser.
HTTP failure/recovery archetype using an intentionally nonexistent public URL.

findings.summary: The public site ignores the user dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The light and dark preference screenshots are pixel-identical (425,026 bytes each); white surfaces remain white under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, controls, imagery and focus states inside prefers-color-scheme or with light-dark().

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM and CSS inspection across the WordPress templates found no view-transition-name or cross-document @view-transition rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin template navigation, with a reduced-motion opt-out.

findings.summary: The long pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation feedback.
findings.evidence: Screenshots and CSS inspection show a static header across pages as long as 12,536 CSS pixels, with no progress indicator or scroll-state query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress indicator or a compacting sticky header using scroll-state/container capabilities with fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation submenus use manually positioned custom structures rather than resilient anchored overlays.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows nested custom ul/div/button menus; no anchor-name, position-anchor, popover, dialog, or details primitives were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover for transient menus and CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks near viewport edges.

findings.summary: Rich navigation controls are built from ad hoc nested lists and divs.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero dialog, popover and details elements; Lighthouse also found invalid direct div/button children in submenu lists.
findings.suggestedFix: Refactor transient menus to buttons plus popover and keep list content structurally valid.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on viewport rules rather than component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across rendered templates found no @container rule even though cards, tabs and navigation components recur in multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable regions and use size-aware @container rules for component layout changes.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are too short for comfortable touch use.
findings.evidence: The evaluate probe found many visible links with 16 to 19 pixel boxes and social links 27 by 19 pixels, below robust touch-target guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the clickable box with block layout or padding while retaining visible focus styles and non-hover affordances.

findings.summary: The signup form does not use native required-state semantics and failed to expose immediate actionable validation.
findings.evidence: All visually required fields reported required=false and empty validationMessage; clicking submit left the captured viewport unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply required and appropriate input types, validate after interaction, focus the first error, and announce a concise error summary.

findings.summary: Homepage lab Core Web Vitals are outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.2 s and CLS 0.226, with performance 52; the trace separately measured LCP 3.65 s on a faster desktop run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the hero LCP asset, reserve stable geometry, and verify mobile LCP and CLS in Lighthouse and field data.

findings.summary: The mobile load shifts substantially in Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured cumulative layout shift 0.226. The short layout observer measured 0, indicating the shift occurs outside that observer window, not that it is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image and dynamic-content space with width/height or aspect-ratio and use stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Heavy script delivery delays interactivity even though individual long tasks are limited.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported interactive at 17.1 s and 434 KiB estimated unused JavaScript; TBT was only 80 ms and the trace saw no long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load page-specific bundles and defer recaptcha and analytics until the relevant interaction or consent.

findings.summary: Critical resource delivery is heavy and contains a long blocking chain.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 68 requests and 3.92 MB transferred, including seven parser-blocking stylesheets and parser-inserted scripts; the largest image alone transferred 1.08 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer noncritical plugin styles/scripts, self-host or consolidate fonts, and prioritize a right-sized hero image.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 434 KiB unused JavaScript and 31 KiB unused CSS, including 67% waste in the theme script and 86% in theme CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Split shared WordPress assets by template and load recaptcha, select2, fancybox and plugin code only where used.

findings.summary: Signup heading and list structure is invalid.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found the form title jumps to h4 and multiple ul elements contain direct div or button children.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sequential heading outline and ensure every ul child is li, placing menu controls outside the list or inside an li.

findings.summary: Image assets are frequently underspecified or oversized.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 19 images without dimensions and 21 oversized images among 63 inspected; the logo natural width was 382 px for a 118 px display width.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, preserve aspect ratio, and provide responsive modern-format sources sized to each slot.

findings.summary: Browser platform diagnostics expose deprecated APIs and missing source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse signup found three deprecated API warnings in the Cloudflare challenge script and a large first-party theme script without a source map.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or configure the challenge integration, remove deprecated calls where controllable, and publish production source maps securely.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a meta description and its title is too generic.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe returned title Clever and description null; Lighthouse SEO scored 92 and failed meta-description.
findings.suggestedFix: Write a unique descriptive title and concise meta description for every public template.

findings.summary: Public organization and article pages lack structured and share-preview metadata on the inspected homepage.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags despite visible organization/product content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter cards; add Article JSON-LD on article templates.

findings.summary: The marketing origin omits baseline security headers and sets insecure cookies.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; the cookies primitive found three Google analytics/visit cookies without Secure and all six cookies with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff and secure cookie attributes; use Lax unless cross-site use is required.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party code load by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found seven third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and Analytics; HAR attributes 706 KB to third parties and Lighthouse signup observed DoubleClick.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential analytics on consent, minimize events, batch delivery, and remove duplicate GTM/gtag paths.

findings.summary: The public student login offers Badge and Password but no visible passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login journey presented only Badge and Password cards; no permission prompt fired on load, and WebAuthn capability exists in the browser.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn where district policy permits while retaining Badge and federated recovery paths.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defense headers are absent on the marketing origin.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP and HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, then verify the login origin independently.

findings.summary: Global-facing templates are not prepared consistently for bidirectional layout.
findings.evidence: The site links Canada, UK/Ireland, Australia/New Zealand and global variants and sets lang=en-US, but CSS inspection counted 1,003 physical left/right declarations and no dir strategy.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties, set dir explicitly where needed, and test representative templates in RTL and expanded translations.

findings.summary: Locale-sensitive article dates are rendered as fixed English text.
findings.evidence: The article template displays OCTOBER 16, 2025 while the global navigation exposes several regions; no locale-aware metadata was observed in rendered output.
findings.suggestedFix: Render machine-readable time elements and format dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the selected locale.

findings.summary: Visually required signup fields are not expressed with native required semantics.
findings.evidence: The form probe found required=false for every visible field and no native validation messages after submit, undermining predictable and assistive error recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints plus post-interaction validation, aria-invalid, linked error text, and a live error summary.

findings.summary: The signup form omits useful autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Name, email, telephone, organization and country inputs all reported empty autocomplete; only a hidden company field used new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Add name, given-name, family-name, email, tel, organization, url, country and organization-title tokens as appropriate.

findings.summary: The homepage image payload is disproportionate and mostly legacy format.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.62 MB of images; the image audit found 47 of 63 in legacy formats, 21 oversized and 25 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, use srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold assets and preserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Page-independent plugin and analytics work is loaded on the homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified 434 KiB unused JavaScript and HAR recorded recaptcha, analytics, select2, PDF, Zoom and fancybox resources on the landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally enqueue WordPress assets per template and delay nonessential third-party work until interaction or consent.

findings.summary: Third-party and media bytes consume a large share without clear first-view value.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 706 KB third-party transfer and 3.92 MB total, including 383 KB recaptcha script and 297 KB GTM before any form interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight budget, defer recaptcha to forms, consolidate analytics, and monitor first/third-party bytes in CI.
